question: A can do a work in 12 days and B can do the same work in 18 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.

Efficiency of A = 3 units/day, Efficiency of B = 2 units/day.

Combined work in 4 days = (3 + 2) × 4 = 20 units.

Remaining work = 36 − 20 = 16 units.

Fraction of work left = 16/36 = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by A to complete the work = 12 days

⇒ Time taken by B to complete the work = 18 days

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of given days

⇒ Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + B) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by A and B working together for 4 days = 5 × 4 = 20 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total Work − Completed Work = 36 − 20 = 16 units.

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining work ÷ Total Work = 16 ÷ 36 = 4/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Time Taken × Efficiency. Efficiency is defined as the work done per unit time.

Combined Work Concept

If person A can do a work in X days and person B can do it in Y days, their combined 1 day work is equal to 1/X + 1/Y.

Work and Wages

If workers complete a job together, the wages are divided in the ratio of the total work done by each individual.

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the same principles as Time and Work, but note that outlet (emptying) pipes have a negative efficiency.
